title: Book 3 — Thalia, Chapter 402
paragraphs: By this way alone is there a known entrance into Egypt. From Phoenicia to the borders of the city of Cadytis belongs to the Syrians known as Palestinians; and from Cadytis — which is a city I suppose not much smaller than Sardis — from this city, the coastal trading stations as far as the city of Ienysos belong to the king of Arabia, and then from Ienysos onward the country belongs to the Syrians again, as far as the Serbonian lake, along which Mount Casion stretches toward the sea. After the Serbonian lake, in which the story is that Typhon is hidden, from this point onward the land is Egypt. The region lying between the city of Ienysos on the one hand and Mount Casion and the Serbonian lake on the other — which is of no small extent, as much as a three days' journey — is grievously lacking in water.
